How necessary do you find the heating mat for pepper germination? I'm trying to go without.

It's not really necessary. When I recently tested a random mix of several varieties, I just put them in a damp napkin in a baggie, and they sprouted in a week or so on the kitchen counter. But if you had superhots, like Carolina Reapers, those can take 4-5 weeks with no bottom heat. ~80ish is good, but if you have lights keeping them warm, that could be fine.

I'd suggest getting them started in damp paper towel or napkin, then carefully transferring them to your growing medium as they germinate. After the C.R. experience, I like knowing they're actually viable and growing, rather than wondering if anything is happening under that soil. But either way can work.

If you were doing cloning work, you'd probably want heat mats, but just the lights should be fine with these seeds.

Nice setup! Indoor grow lights are perfect for starting seeds. I use the same wire shelving. I advise boot trays to put underneath your seedling trays so that the excess water can drain onto the tray.

Also, get a simple electric outlet timer so that you don't have to manually turn the lights on and off (it gets old fast, trust me). Another tip is to check with your electric company to see if they have a lower rate for "off-peak" hours. For example, my electricity rate is lower between 10pm and 6am, so I have my lights turn on at nighttime hours to save money on electricity.
